blocks.text: Buying an Acreage or Hobby Farm in Langley Township: ALR, Rural Plan and Well Water Basics

parts.t: About 75% of Langley Township's land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR),

. If you're picturing a few acres and a barn, the ALR will likely shape what you can build and do. Here's a plain-language overview, plus what came up at a rural all-candidates event ahead of the October 17, 2026 municipal election.

blocks.text: Buying acreage in Langley: start with the ALR

parts.t: The ALR is a provincial land-use zone where agriculture is the priority use. The Agricultural Land Commission (ALC)
a few points often surprise buyers:
Zoning can't allow what ALR rules don't without ALC approval, and local governments can be stricter.
Minimum lot sizes in zoning don't mean you can subdivide.
Subdivision in the ALR is tightly controlled.
Existing buildings or uses aren't proof of approval.
They may not comply with ALR rules.
, since a title's ALR notation isn't definitive. The rules apply only to the part of a property inside the ALR.
Expect farm noise, dust and odours.
Normal farm practices are protected under BC's Right to Farm legislation.

blocks.text: ALR rules in Langley Township: houses, suites and additional residences

parts.t: page sets out the provincial limits:
Most ALR properties can have one principal residence of up to 500 m² without an application, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill, including the driveway.
Only inside the principal residence, if local bylaws allow.
One additional residence, in some cases.

It must be detached, and the property can have only one residence when construction begins. It can be up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on larger ones, and only if the main home is within the ALC's permitted size. It needn't be for farm help, and any fill needs a Notice of Intent to the ALC.
needs a Non-Adhering Residential Use application. The local government reviews it first, and approval isn't guaranteed.
Local governments can further restrict the number, size and siting of homes, so check what the Township allows on a specific property.

parts.t: Farming, raising livestock (including horses) and many farm-related activities are permitted farm uses in the ALR,
. Some non-farm uses, such as a home-based business, are permitted with conditions (local governments can prohibit some of them); others need an ALC application.

blocks.text: Langley Township's Rural Plan and zoning

parts.t: (Bylaw No. 3250, adopted July 12, 1993 and amended since) has a primary goal of enhancing agricultural viability, while also retaining countryside character. Most of the rural area is designated Agriculture/Countryside, with a minimum lot size of 8 ha (19.8 acres), subject to ALC approval.
sets permitted uses, lot coverage and building restrictions, which vary by property. The Township's
mapping tool shows a property's zoning and, under the Planning layer, its rural land use designation.
A Rural Plan update isn't formally underway. The Township's Agricultural Advisory Committee recommended one on September 24, 2025, and Council
on November 3, 2025. On April 22, 2026, staff told the committee they were working on terms of reference. As of October 1, 2026, there's no published timeline or public engagement page.

Irrigation, commercial or industrial use requires a water licence, with a one-time application fee of at least $250 plus annual rentals.

blocks.text: What Township candidates heard ahead of the October 17 election

parts.t: On September 22, the Langley Farmers Institute hosted an all-candidates event at Coghlan Hall,
by the Langley Advance Times. A majority of council candidates and both mayoral candidates took part, rotating through small-group stations on:

items.t: Enforcement of bylaws in agricultural areas
Truck parking in relation to the Rural Plan
The Board of Variance and agricultural issues

parts.t: The Farmers Institute's Amanda Smith said the message to candidates was, "These issues are coming to you."

For context from Township records: the Zoning Bylaw lets most rural properties park up to three commercial vehicles as an accessory to residential use, and the Township has used tickets and court injunctions against unauthorized trucking. In June 2026, Council approved terms of reference for an Agricultural Bylaw Review Task Force, which runs until November 30, 2026. In February 2026, a provincial groundwater specialist told Council that 21 mapped aquifers overlap the Township, where common issues include declining water levels and contamination. The
can consider minor zoning relaxations, such as setbacks, for undue hardship, but it isn't an appeal route for land use or density.
General voting day is Saturday, October 17, 2026, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., with advance voting October 6 to 10, per the
. Mail-in voting isn't available. The October 24 provincial election is a separate vote.
Is my Langley property in the ALR?
Can I build a second home on ALR land?

Possibly one small detached additional residence, if the property has only one home when construction begins and the main home is within the ALC's size limit. The Township can be stricter, so check with the Township and the ALC.
Can I run an Airbnb on an ALR acreage?
A bed-and-breakfast of up to four bedrooms in the home you live in is allowed (stays of 30 days or less). Whole-house short-term rentals need ALC approval, and Township rules also apply.
Do I need a licence for my well?

Not for household use; irrigation and other non-domestic use need a provincial licence. If you connect to Township water, the well must be decommissioned within 30 days unless you apply to keep it for agricultural use.
Not just because zoning lists a minimum lot size. ALR subdivision is tightly controlled, and each new rural lot needs a proven well water supply. Check with the Township and the ALC.
